instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: As a mid-sized clinical laboratory, Pulse performs high-volume hematology and molecular diagnostics, serving physicians requiring rapid turnaround times for critical patient data. The company is currently focused on optimizing existing workflows and leveraging current technology to maintain service quality while exploring opportunities in molecular profiling and next-generation assay development.
answers.pastInitiatives: The company has not undertaken any systematic innovation or transformation programs; operational model changes have been minimal over the past three years. While leadership recognizes the necessity of modernization to secure future growth, there is no defined framework for identifying, scoping, or funding new projects.
answers.strategicGoals: Growth is our existential mandate. We are losing market share to faster-moving competitors and need to reignite our growth trajectory. We are willing to make significant strategic bets—potentially including M&A, new product lines, or geographic expansion—provided they have a credible path to meaningful revenue contribution within 18 months.
answers.additionalContext: Internal resistance to change is high due to the lean resources and lack of a structured innovation pipeline. The company lacks standardized metrics to measure the success or failure of nascent ideas.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Diagnostic Stream Optimization
opportunities.rationale: Developing a proprietary AI algorithm to analyze peripheral blood smears and identify subtle hematological patterns could significantly reduce manual interpretation time while improving diagnostic accuracy. This would create a defensible, high-value service that differentiates the lab.

first_actions: Conduct feasibility study on existing data infrastructure for AI training.
Assign 2 engineers to build a minimum viable product (MVP) model focused on differential cell counting.
resources_needed: Training/licensing costs for specialized ML models
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 15% reduction in sample interpretation time within 6 months.
milestones: Month 1: Data pipeline established and initial model training begins.
Month 3: Internal validation of MVP accuracy against expert reviews.

opportunities.title: Core Workflow Automation Pilot
opportunities.rationale: Implementing targeted automation for sample tracking and basic data entry in high-volume areas will improve operational efficiency. This is a low-risk, incremental step that frees up staff time without requiring major capital expenditure.

first_actions: Identify the top 3 most time-consuming manual tasks.
Procure and integrate off-the-shelf workflow management software.
execution_plan.success_metric: Decrease average sample processing time by 10%.
milestones: Month 2: Pilot implementation in one specific department.
Month 4: Full rollout planning based on pilot results.

next_steps.action: Establish a minimal, formal innovation pipeline (Idea submission -> Screening -> Resource allocation).
Allocate a dedicated $50k seed budget specifically for the AI diagnostic pilot project.
Conduct quarterly performance reviews tied to innovation KPIs (not just operational ones).

key_weaknesses: Lack of a formal innovation process, leading to zero systematic R&D.
Critical constraints on budget (5%) preventing significant capital expenditures or staffing changes.
Low digital maturity (Level 1) resulting in heavy reliance on manual workflows and spreadsheets.
Internal culture prioritizing maintenance over proactive growth/innovation.
